franz-brentano.oneLineEn: Revived intentionality; descriptive psychology linked Aristotle, scholasticism, and Husserl.

alexius-meinong.oneLineEn: Founded object theory, arguing that non-existent objects have their own being and shaping ontology debates.

ernst-cassirer.oneLineEn: Founded the philosophy of symbolic forms, uniting myth, language, and science as human symbolization.

josiah-royce.oneLineEn: American absolute idealist and philosopher of community, centering ethics on loyalty.

george-santayana.oneLineEn: Bridged naturalism, skepticism, and aesthetics through The Life of Reason and Realms of Being.

fh-bradley.oneLineEn: British absolute idealist; internal relations became a main target of the Russell-Moore revolt.

th-green.oneLineEn: Source of British neo-Hegelianism and new liberalism; ethical state and positive freedom reworked liberty.

georg-simmel.oneLineEn: Formal sociology and cultural philosophy analyzing modern experience via interaction forms and money.

max-scheler.oneLineEn: Built phenomenological value ethics around material values and personhood against Kantian formalism.

gabriel-marcel.oneLineEn: Christian existentialist who distinguished mystery from problem and developed a phenomenology of hope.

jose-ortega-y-gasset.oneLineEn: Advocate of ratiovitalism and perspectivism; The Revolt of the Masses critiques mass society.

miguel-de-unamuno.oneLineEn: The Tragic Sense of Life stages the irreconcilable conflict between reason and faith.

giovanni-gentile.oneLineEn: Founder of actual idealism; pure act of thinking as sole reality, diverging from Croce.

rg-collingwood.oneLineEn: Philosophy of history and question-and-answer logic: all history is re-enactment of thought now.

michael-oakeshott.oneLineEn: Opposed political rationalism with practical knowledge; gave British conservatism a philosophical voice.

jl-austin.oneLineEn: Source of speech-act theory; How to Do Things with Words moved language from meaning to action.

pf-strawson.oneLineEn: Individuals established descriptive metaphysics, reconnecting Kant with analytic philosophy.

michael-dummett.oneLineEn: Theory of meaning and anti-realism; reread Frege via assertibility conditions.

thomas-nagel.oneLineEn: Author of 'What is it like to be a bat?'; challenged reductionism from the subjective point of view.

georges-sorel.oneLineEn: Reflections on Violence made social myth and revolutionary syndicalism a heterodox Marxist path.

nicolai-hartmann.oneLineEn: New ontology mediating phenomenology and metaphysics via stratified structure of the real.

paul-natorp.oneLineEn: Core Marburg neo-Kantian who carried epistemology into social pedagogy.

heinrich-rickert.oneLineEn: Refined cultural-science methodology via value-relation; direct background to Weber's method.

ernst-troeltsch.oneLineEn: Historicism and philosophy of religion at the crossroads of Dilthey, Weber, and theological modernity.

maurice-blondel.oneLineEn: Action traces the inner logic of action toward transcendence, opening modern French Catholic thought.

ci-lewis.oneLineEn: Conceptual pragmatism and modal logic; strict implication answered material-implication paradoxes.

frank-ramsey.oneLineEn: Early hub of truth, probability, decision, and economics; foundational work despite death at twenty-six.

susan-stebbing.oneLineEn: Britain's first woman philosophy professor; Thinking to Some Purpose spread logical analysis for public reasoning.

cd-broad.oneLineEn: Cambridge synthesizer of mind, ethics, and metaphysics, known for fine classification and moderate eclecticism.

nelson-goodman.oneLineEn: Reframed induction with the grue paradox and extended symbol-system theory into aesthetics.

david-armstrong.oneLineEn: Australian materialist whose realist universals and mind-brain identity form a metaphysical system.

jjc-smart.oneLineEn: Defended mind-brain identity theory and consequentialism under thoroughgoing scientific realism.

ruth-barcan-marcus.oneLineEn: Pioneer of quantified modal logic; the Barcan formula paved later modal semantics.

john-mcdowell.oneLineEn: Mind and World holds experience already conceptual, reconnecting analysis with Hegel.

robert-brandom.oneLineEn: Inferentialist semantics: meaning rests on practices of giving and asking for reasons.

alvin-plantinga.oneLineEn: Reformed epistemology and modal ontological argument; theistic belief can be properly basic.

richard-swinburne.oneLineEn: Bayesian probabilistic case for theism; contemporary Anglo-American natural theology.

rm-hare.oneLineEn: Prescriptivism: moral judgments are both prescriptive and universalizable.

judith-jarvis-thomson.oneLineEn: Violinist argument and trolley problem reshaped applied ethics' case tradition.

alain-locke.oneLineEn: Philosophical interpreter of the Harlem Renaissance; argued value pluralism across cultural difference.

leo-strauss.oneLineEn: Revived classical political philosophy and reread the ancients-moderns quarrel via esoteric writing.

judith-shklar.oneLineEn: Rebuilt liberalism around the liberalism of fear and a priority concern with cruelty.

hans-jonas.oneLineEn: The Imperative of Responsibility set ethical demands on technological civilization for future generations.

eric-voegelin.oneLineEn: Diagnosed modernity through political religion and philosophy of order, treating Gnosticism as the disease.

alexandre-kojeve.oneLineEn: Lectures on the Phenomenology via master-slave dialectic shaped a generation of French thinkers.

louis-althusser.oneLineEn: Structuralist Marxist of ideological state apparatuses and the epistemological break.

jan-patocka.oneLineEn: Czech phenomenologist and Charter 77 spokesman; care of the soul as historical existence.

leszek-kolakowski.oneLineEn: Author of Main Currents of Marxism; moved from revisionism to religious questioning of utopia.

cornelius-castoriadis.oneLineEn: Made social imaginary institution and autonomy theory a heterodox current in Western Marxism.

cournot.oneLineEn: Linked positivism and French epistemology via probability, economics, and theories of chance.

poincare.oneLineEn: Conventionalism: geometric axioms are neither empirical nor a priori, but conventions.

duhem.oneLineEn: Duhem thesis: hypotheses cannot be tested in isolation; paved the way for Quinean holism.

koyre.oneLineEn: From the Closed World to the Infinite Universe rewrote Scientific Revolution history, shaping Kuhn.

bachelard.oneLineEn: Recast history of science through epistemological break and obstacle, plus a poetics of material imagination.

canguilhem.oneLineEn: The Normal and the Pathological rewrote philosophy of medicine via vital normativity; Foucault's mentor.

badiou.oneLineEn: Being and Event builds ontology and an evental conception of truth on set theory.

raymond-aron.oneLineEn: Defended liberalism via The Opium of the Intellectuals and philosophy of history; long debate with Sartre.

etienne-gilson.oneLineEn: Reread Aquinas around esse and advanced the historiography of medieval philosophy.

emmanuel-mounier.oneLineEn: Started the personalist movement and launched Esprit around personhood and community.

jaimini.oneLineEn: Jaimini is traditionally credited with the Mīmāṃsā Sūtra, grounding early Mīmāṃsā ritual hermeneutics.

patanjali.oneLineEn: Yoga tradition credits him with the Yoga Sūtras, systematizing eight-limbed practice.

kanada.oneLineEn: Vaiśeṣika tradition credits him with the Vaiśeṣika Sūtra, grounding atomism and categories.
